headline: Benchmarking sequencing tools for transcript and transposable element quantification
label: Sequencing Analysis Tool Benchmarks
summary: Benchmarks and automated pipelines test how reliably sequencing-based tools quantify transcripts, transposable elements, and RNA-protein interactions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the evaluation and construction of computational tools for sequencing data, with accuracy assessed against real data, simulations, or reproducibility criteria. A locus-level transposable element benchmark for short-read scRNA-seq compares SoloTE and Stellarscope using real data and read-level simulations, while a systematic benchmark compares PacBio Kinnex long-read RNA-seq with Illumina short-read data for transcript-level quantification. Exclusion-set work finds ENCODE Blacklist sets poorly reproducible and proposes sponge decoy sequences with T2T-CHM13 to reduce alignment artifacts. Other items deliver automated tooling: PARANOiD for iCLIP read analysis, RAPseq for large-scale RBP-RNA interaction identification, and a deep learning predictor of RNA G-quadruplex-binding proteins (86% accuracy, 2160 candidates, G4REP server). A 1,515-dataset reanalysis of translational buffering is methodologically related through uniform reprocessing. What is new is systematic assessment of tools against real data, with reference and decoy choices treated as analysis variables.
